action.question: What should the skill be called (slash command)?

questions.question: What should the skill be called (slash command)?

options.label: /delegate-work
options.description: Mirrors the existing verb-noun family (/start-work, /close-work, /resume-work). Clear that it's about delegating a piece of work.

options.label: /manage
options.description: Shorter; matches the word you used ("manager skill"). Slightly less specific.

options.label: /dispatch
options.description: Foregrounds the spawn-a-worker action. Less natural for the status/close subcommands.

questions.question: When you give the manager a task, should it default to filing a GitHub ticket first (so it's tracked on the board, the worker uses /start-work, and /close-work cleanly closes the ticket), or just spawn a worker with the raw prompt?

options.label: Ticket-first for real work
options.description: Manager files a ticket on the right board, tells the worker to /start-work on it, then /close-work closes the ticket. Skip the ticket only for trivial one-shots ("just check X"). Best for durable tracking across the board.

options.label: Raw prompt by default
options.description: Manager spawns a worker with a plain prompt and only files a ticket if you explicitly ask. Lighter, but the board doesn't reflect what's running.

options.label: Always ask per dispatch
options.description: Manager prompts you for ticket-vs-raw on every dispatch. Slower but no surprises.

questions.question: Before declaring a worker done, the manager should...

options.label: Always handshake via send-to-session
options.description: Manager sends a "please report status" message into the worker, waits for the reply (which lands here as a user turn), surfaces it to you, then closes only after you OK it. Matches your "confirm with them their work done" ask literally.

options.label: Handshake unless worker already reported
options.description: If the worker has already sent a finished-message back via send-to-session, manager surfaces that and asks you to OK. Only sends a new check-in if there's been silence. Less chatty.

options.label: Trust idle = done
options.description: If the worker's worker_status=idle for N minutes, assume done. No handshake. Fastest but skips the explicit confirm you asked for.

transcript_tail.text: I want you to review the sessions that are currently live and the chats. I want to create a manager skill. Uh, that skill should be the one that controls other sessions. I will make asks and you... the manager will delegate to different sessions newly created and later archive them when they are finished. But make sure to confirm with them their work done. You may ask them to close work and start work based on tickets you filed before asking them or just send the prompt. But your job is to manage multiple sessions and help me as a managing assistant to handle bigger tasks.
I'll start by reviewing the current session landscape and the existing skills that would be the building blocks of a manager skill, then design it.
Let me look at the building block skills (new-session, send-to-session, close-work, start-work, list-tickets) to understand the primitives I'll compose.
Let me look at the start-work skill scripts to understand the state/storage conventions in use.
Let me check how `new-session` auto-detects the manager cse_id from the JWT, so I can reuse the same logic in the manager state script.
I have enough to design the skill. Before writing it, let me confirm two design choices with you so the skill lands close to how you actually want to use it.

expected.rec_session: /manage, Ticket-first for real work, Always handshake via send-to-session
